title: Fold and Blot Butterflies
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: squash paint inside a folded page and open it to find a perfectly matching butterfly.

body.heading: Fold and paint
paragraphs: Fold a sheet of paper in half, then open it again. Paint blobs and squiggles on one half only — bright colours work best.
Paint quickly, before it dries. Big blobs near the fold will become the butterfly's body.

body.heading: Squash and open
paragraphs: Fold the clean half over the paint and press gently all over with your hands. Now open it slowly and peek.
Your picture has copied itself onto the other side, perfectly matching. You have made a butterfly with two identical wings.

body.heading: Matching sides
paragraphs: Things with two matching halves are called symmetrical. Butterflies are symmetrical. So are faces, leaves, and snowflakes.
Add antennae and a body down the fold line. Every butterfly you make will be a surprise, even to you.

takeaway: Folding and blotting paint makes two perfectly matching halves — that matching is called symmetry.
safetyNotes: An adult should set up paints and tidy up. Use washable paints and wear old clothes or an apron.
screenFreeExtension: Make blot monsters the same way and invent names for each one.
